question: 在雇主雇用不可分割的勞動者、政府可依雇用組合或薪資設計稅補的市場中，財政措施何時會保留或恢復需求替代性及其均衡基礎？
scope: Post-unblinding audit of the same finite indivisible-worker, set- and salary-dependent fiscal-policy question. The original b03 blind survey remains archived unchanged.
contribution_statement: Directly corresponding published article exists. The r01 manuscript is a historical reconstruction/development exercise, not a novel journal submission.

searches.query: Kelso Crawford 1982 job matching coalition formation gross substitutes Journal of Political Economy
Hatfield Milgrom 2005 matching with contracts American Economic Review substitutes wages
arxiv 2023 gross substitutes demand indivisible goods competitive equilibrium discrete convexity
site:nber.org/papers 2023 matching with contracts substitutes equilibrium wages

nearest_works.title: Job Matching with Subsidy and Taxation
nearest_works.question: Which bundle- and salary-dependent fiscal transfers preserve or restore substitutes in indivisible-worker matching markets?
nearest_works.estimand_or_theorem: Necessary-and-sufficient preservation classes for simple, group-structured and salary-dependent transfers, and a restoration criterion.
nearest_works.difference: The r01 paper proves only narrower cases and one bounded two-worker policy result; the original question and core results are already published.
nearest_works.prior_bottleneck: Fiscal policy may destroy substitutes that underpin equilibrium existence.
nearest_works.innovation: Characterises policy classes preserving substitutes and when cardinally concave transfers restore it.
nearest_works.why_field_cares: Identifies restrictions on taxes and subsidies that retain the demand structure used in market design.
nearest_works.validation: Publisher full text and online appendix inspected after b03 manuscript lock; see r01/overlap-audit.md.
nearest_works.influence_or_reuse: Direct historical reconstruction target; rules out novelty for original broad question.

nearest_works.title: Job Matching, Coalition Formation, and Gross Substitutes
nearest_works.question: Stable job matching with indivisible heterogeneous workers.
nearest_works.estimand_or_theorem: Equilibrium existence and stability under firm gross substitutes.
nearest_works.method_or_proof: Competitive wage adjustment and matching-theoretic existence argument.
nearest_works.difference: Provides the untaxed gross-substitutes benchmark; does not classify a fiscal transformation.
nearest_works.prior_bottleneck: Discrete worker choices undermine ordinary convexity arguments.
nearest_works.innovation: Imposes firm gross substitutes on worker demand to recover equilibrium and stability.
nearest_works.why_field_cares: Makes a rigorous equilibrium foundation possible despite indivisible labor.
nearest_works.validation: Original Econometrica article; author-hosted scan acquired, abstract and bibliographic metadata checked.
nearest_works.influence_or_reuse: Canonical baseline for gross substitutes in labor matching.

nearest_works.title: Matching with Contracts
nearest_works.question: Stable matching when agreements include contractual terms such as wages.
nearest_works.estimand_or_theorem: Contract substitutability and law of aggregate demand results.
nearest_works.method_or_proof: Matching-with-contracts choice functions and cumulative offer algorithm.
nearest_works.difference: General contract framework may already absorb wage-dependent policy; specific policy primitives are not classified there.
nearest_works.prior_bottleneck: Separate matching and auction models lacked a common contract object.
nearest_works.innovation: Uses bilateral contracts and substitutable choice functions as the shared formal object.
nearest_works.why_field_cares: Transfers stability and incentive insights across labor matching and other contract markets.
nearest_works.validation: Original AER article and author-hosted full text acquired; abstract checked.
nearest_works.influence_or_reuse: Direct benchmark for any wage-contract formulation.

nearest_works.title: Discrete Convex Analysis: A Tool for Economics and Game Theory
nearest_works.question: How discrete convex analysis supports economic equilibrium and games with indivisibilities.
nearest_works.estimand_or_theorem: Connections of M-natural-concavity and gross substitutes, with equilibrium tools.
nearest_works.method_or_proof: Survey of exchange axioms, conjugacy, separation, and fixed-point methods.
nearest_works.difference: Mathematical toolkit rather than classification of fiscal transformations on firm demand.
nearest_works.prior_bottleneck: Continuous convex analysis does not directly handle indivisible bundles.
nearest_works.innovation: Presents discrete convexity as a reusable bridge to substitution and equilibrium.
nearest_works.why_field_cares: Provides tractable exchange conditions and equilibrium methods for discrete economies.
nearest_works.validation: arXiv original metadata and first pages checked; complete PDF acquired.
nearest_works.influence_or_reuse: Reference for checking whether proposed policy conditions merely restate known closure properties.
nearest_works.frontier_case: If policy-modified value is M-natural-concave, established results may cover the substitution step.
nearest_works.selection_reason: Direct mathematical overlap and duplication risk.

nearest_works.title: Existence of a Competitive Equilibrium with Substitutes, with Applications to Matching and Discrete Choice Models
nearest_works.question: Existence and uniqueness of competitive equilibrium in general systems with substitutes.
nearest_works.estimand_or_theorem: Weak substitutes, pivotal substitutes, and responsiveness sufficient for existence.
nearest_works.method_or_proof: Nonparametric equilibrium theorem and algorithm with matching/discrete-choice applications.
nearest_works.difference: General competitive-system criteria, not a fiscal policy transformation in an indivisible employer-worker model.
nearest_works.prior_bottleneck: Uniqueness results did not automatically establish existence.
nearest_works.innovation: Adds a sufficient existence framework and constructive algorithm.
nearest_works.why_field_cares: Broadens equilibrium analysis across matching and discrete choice.
nearest_works.validation: arXiv original metadata and first pages checked; complete PDF acquired.
nearest_works.influence_or_reuse: Potential off-the-shelf existence theorem if its assumptions map to the proposed model.
nearest_works.frontier_case: If transformed demand satisfies the paper’s three conditions, its theorem may cover the equilibrium step.
nearest_works.selection_reason: Discussed and cited in the manuscript under the ChenEtAl2023 bibliography key.

nearest_works.title: Labor Market Matching, Wages, and Amenities
nearest_works.question: Labor market matching, wages, and amenities with worker and firm heterogeneity.
nearest_works.estimand_or_theorem: Model-consistent identification of heterogeneous labor market primitives.
nearest_works.method_or_proof: Structural equilibrium model estimated using Swedish matched worker-firm data.
nearest_works.difference: Empirical matching model rather than set-demand or fiscal gross-substitutes theorem.
nearest_works.prior_bottleneck: Joint worker and firm heterogeneity complicates interpretation of wages and sorting.
nearest_works.innovation: Combines equilibrium contracting with identified heterogeneity and administrative data.
nearest_works.why_field_cares: Makes wage and amenity mechanisms measurable in a broad labor market model.
nearest_works.validation: NBER original landing page and first pages checked; complete PDF acquired.
nearest_works.influence_or_reuse: Context for the limits of a stylized indivisible-worker theory.
nearest_works.frontier_case: If a theory claims direct labor-market applicability, heterogeneity and amenities may limit that interpretation.
nearest_works.selection_reason: Contextual empirical matching paper; not used as theorem evidence in this historical theory reconstruction.

limitations: This is a post-unblinding decision. It cannot retroactively make the b03 author-side survey non-blind or change the frozen historical score.
One broad browser result accidentally exposed a possibly restricted title. Only its URL and time are recorded in a separate contamination log; no content was opened or used.
Browser search-result records are curated transcriptions; full raw arXiv search pages could not be acquired due timeout and rate limiting.
Only abstracts and first pages of acquired full texts were checked; proofs and backward/forward citation chains were not fully audited.
